Coupled Technique(s).cell: Laser-ablation MC-ICP-MS — the same NEPTUNE, with a NewWave UP213 laser, "such that laser ablation and solution aspiration can be operated simultaneously"

Coupling Description.cell: Functional: the laser is connected directly to the spray chamber so ablated particles mix with 2% HNO3 and are "effectively analyzed as a wet plasma ensuring that ablated aerosols are closely matrix-matched to solution standards". Sequence: interchangeable — "Our setup allows for interchangeable bulk and in situ S isotope measurement"
Coupling Description.value: Functional: the laser is connected directly to the spray chamber so ablated particles mix with 2% HNO3 and are "effectively analyzed as a wet plasma ensuring that ablated aerosols are closely matrix-matched to solution standards". Sequence: interchangeable

Target Material.cell: sulfide; sulfate; elemental sulfur; seawater — Table 3: Ag2S, ZnS, pyrite, pyrrhotite, anhydrite, Fe(III) sulfate, elemental S and modern seawater

Sampling Unit Type.cell: Purified solution aliquot — "Less than 50 mg of sample was accurately weighed"; "A precise solution volume, corresponding to 500 µg of S" taken for column purification

Sample Preparation Method.cell: Less than 50 mg weighed, digested, S purified on AG50-X8 cation exchange and diluted with 2% HNO3 to a 50 ppm S stock; for laser work, a 2 mm thick polished section on a petrographic slide — §2.1–2.2
Sample Preparation Method.value: Less than 50 mg weighed, digested, S purified on AG50-X8 cation exchange and diluted with 2% HNO3 to a 50 ppm S stock; for laser work, a 2 mm thick polished section on a petrographic slide

Digestion Acid(s).cell: HNO3 attack: 50% HNO3; HNO3–HCl digestion: concentrated HNO3 + 50% HCl; re-dissolution: 2% HNO3 — §2.2

Digestion Step.cell: HNO3 attack (5 ml 50% HNO3, hot plate below 70 °C, to dryness); HNO3–HCl digestion (3 ml concentrated HNO3 + 2 ml 50% HCl, sealed PTFE vessel, 70 °C, to dryness); re-dissolution (4 ml 2% HNO3, AgCl from Ag2S removed by centrifugation) — §2.2

Digestion Temperature.cell: HNO3 attack: below 70 °C; HNO3–HCl digestion: 70 °C; re-dissolution: N — §2.2

Final Solution Matrix.cell: all: 2% HNO3 — a 50 ppm S stock (§2.2); standards at 20 ppm S

Sample Aliquot Mass or Volume.cell: <50 mg weighed; 500 µg S taken for column purification
Sample Aliquot Mass or Volume.value: <50 mg weighed; 500 µg S taken for column purification

Chromatographic Separation Applied.cell: Yes, AG50-X8 (H+) cation exchange, 2.5 ml resin conditioned with 1.4 N HNO3; S and oxyanions pass, matrix retained; yield 98 ± 4% (§2.2)
Chromatographic Separation Applied.value: Yes, AG50-X8 (H+) cation exchange, 2.5 ml resin conditioned with 1.4 N HNO3; S and oxyanions pass, matrix retained; yield 98 ± 4% (§2.2)

Isotope Dilution Spike.cell: N/A — no isotope dilution spike; mass bias handled by standard-sample bracketing or internal normalization

ICP-MS Type.cell: Multi-collector sector-field ICP-MS [all columns state "multi-collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer"]
ICP-MS Type.value: Multi-collector sector-field ICP-MS [all columns state "multi-collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer"]

Faraday Cup Array Configuration.cell: Nine Faraday cups — "equipped with nine Faraday Cups" (p.3); Table 1 gives detection system "Faraday cups" and acquisition mode "Static, analogue detectors" (p.3). No ion counter stated

Spray Chamber Type and Cooling Temperatu.cell: SSI cyclonic spray dual chamber, Elemental Scientific, Inc.; cooling not stated
Spray Chamber Type and Cooling Temperatu.value: SSI cyclonic spray dual chamber, Elemental Scientific, Inc.; cooling not stated

Desolvation System.cell: all: none — 'passing solutions through a desolvating nebulizer to obtain dry plasma conditions is not viable for bulk analysis' (§2.3)

Plasma Thermal Mode.cell: all: wet plasma — solutions 'introduced as a wet aerosol (in 2% HNO3)' (Fig. 1)

Monitored Masses.key: defines: monitored property per target species
Monitored Masses.cell: 32S, 33S, 34S → S — §2.4; ³⁶S not reported because of its low abundance and Ar interferences

Reported Variables and Units.cell: δ34S, δ33S — ‰ on the V-CDT scale (§2.4)

Baseline Measurement Approach.cell: 5 s at the beginning of each analysis with the ion beams deflected — §2.4
Baseline Measurement Approach.value: 5 s at the beginning of each analysis with the ion beams deflected

Wash Time Between Samples.cell: 2 min — Table 1; 4 min after laser analyses

Analysis Sequence.cell: Each sample bracketed by standards analysed immediately before and after, with 2% HNO3 blanks aspirated periodically through the session — §2.4, §3.2
Analysis Sequence.value: Each sample bracketed by standards analysed immediately before and after, with 2% HNO3 blanks aspirated periodically through the session

Internal Standard Element.cell: N/A — mass bias corrected by standard-sample bracketing, internal normalization or a double spike rather than by an added internal standard element

Internal Standard Concentration.cell: N/A — no added internal standard element

Doubly-Charged Species Monitor.cell: N — ⁶⁴Zn²⁺, ⁶⁶Zn²⁺ and ⁶⁸Zn²⁺ are listed as interferences on the S masses, Table 2, p.4, and resolved by mass resolution, p.5; no M²⁺ tuning monitor or production ratio is stated

Mass Bias Correction Strategy.cell: Standard-sample bracketing with matrix-matched purified S solutions, linear interpolation between the biases of two neighbouring standards, sample and standard matched within ~20% in intensity at ~10 V — §2.4, §3.1
Mass Bias Correction Strategy.value: Standard-sample bracketing with matrix-matched purified S solutions, linear interpolation between the biases of two neighbouring standards, sample and standard matched within ~20% in intensity at ~10 V

Blank / Background Correction Method.cell: Average on-peak-zero background from periodic 2% HNO3 blanks, measured on the low-mass shoulder, subtracted per isotope off-line — ~30–50 mV on ³²S (§2.4, §3.1)
Blank / Background Correction Method.value: Average on-peak-zero background from periodic 2% HNO3 blanks, measured on the low-mass shoulder, subtracted per isotope off-line

Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach.cell: None, no automatic 2σ rejection of outlying cycles — 'Automatic rejection of outlying cycles (2σ outlier criterion) offered within the NEPTUNE software is not performed' (§2.4)
Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach.value: None, no automatic 2σ rejection of outlying cycles

Spectral Interference Corrections Applie.cell: Y, molecular interferences resolved in high resolution — ³²S¹H on mass 33 unresolved
Spectral Interference Corrections Applie.value: Y, molecular interferences resolved in high resolution

Interference Correction Method.cell: 32S, 34S: resolved in high resolution on the interference-free low-mass shoulder, hydride effects corrected by standard-sample bracketing; 33S: as for 32S, but 32S1H (>10% of mass 33) is unresolved — hydride rate checked per measurement from (³³S + ³²SH)/³²S against ³⁴S/³²S (§3.1)

Uncertainty Level.cell: 1σ internal precision for individual analyses, 2σ external reproducibility for replicates — §2.4
Uncertainty Level.value: 1σ internal precision for individual analyses, 2σ external reproducibility for replicates

Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.cell: Rule: data showing mass-bias drift greater than ~0.5‰ during an individual sample are discarded; no count stated — 'Data that show clear and large mass bias drift (greater than ∼0.5‰) during individual samples should be discarded'
Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.value: Rule: data showing mass-bias drift greater than ~0.5‰ during an individual sample are discarded; no count stated
